category_title: Unmotivated rising first graders with significant letter-sound recognition deficits and high interest in specific machinery
minimal_context: Derek is sitting in the Literacy Corner during a one-on-one tutoring session, tasked with writing his name and a sentence of his choice in his reflection journal.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please write your first and last name in your reflection journal, and then write a sentence of your choice.

STUDENT: I don't know all the letters.

TUTOR: Just try your best to write what you can.

STUDENT: I want to write a sentence about a green tractor. But I don't know how to make the sentence.

TUTOR: Go ahead and try writing the words down on the paper.

STUDENT: I can't do it! I don't know how to form the letters or write the simple sight words.

options.A: Compromise, negotiate situations, and share decisions and power with Derek instead of imposing control during the writing task.
options.B: Set a standard of interacting with Derek at a ratio of four positive interactions to one negative interaction during the session.
options.C: Provide a template with simple sentences for Derek to complete his ideas and draw related illustrations in his reflection journal.
options.D: Alter interpretations of the given behavior during the session, viewing it as a desire for social interaction rather than simple noncompliance.
